developments.title: OBR energy-import shock, real incomes and fiscal exposure
developments.facts: The official October outlook describes a negative energy terms-of-trade shock. developments.title: Treasury auction and NYFed results distinguish awards from caps
developments.facts: TreasuryDirect confirms CUSIP 91282CRS2 is a two-year floating-rate note: $30 billion offered, $30.0000248 billion par awarded inside the offering plus $3.3335517 billion outside it, bid-to-cover 3.05 and high discount margin 0.038%. Its October 28 11:30 AM Eastern close is distinct from the record update. The 17-week bill reports bid-to-cover 3.08; these do not establish FX flows. NYFed October 28 results show $3 million accepted in each of its two standing-repo operations and $176 million in reverse repo; routine implementation is not QE. These provider/time snapshots are not interchangeable or a directly refreshed curve. CIBC/Desjardins favour another hike in January and 2.75% peak, illustrating forecast disagreement. Stronger growth/income and a possible longer cycle are support; the reported negative near-term path repricing is material opposition to a current strengthening claim.

developments.title: US Q3 domestic demand remains strong; monthly core persistence offsets quarterly disinflation
developments.facts: Q3 advance real GDP grew 3.4% at a seasonally adjusted annualised rate, versus Q2 2.2% and the attributed web survey 3.2%; the broker-model forecast was 1.4% and is not consensus. Real final sales to private domestic purchasers rose 4.9%, versus 4.6%, supporting genuine private demand apart from inventories, trade and government. Investment included inventory accumulation and information-processing equipment. Exports fell and imports rose; neither is described as an independent bullish vote. Gross domestic purchases prices rose 3.0% annualised, a different measure from the GDP deflator. Quarterly PCE inflation slowed to 2.1% from 5.0%, core to 2.5% from 3.3%. Separately, September monthly headline PCE rose 0.5%, 3.6% y/y; core rose 0.3%, 3.1% y/y. Monthly core matched the 0.3% web survey but exceeded the 0.2% broker forecast. August monthly core was revised from 0.2% to 0.3%. Personal income rose 0.2%, nominal spending 0.5%, real spending less than 0.1% (rounded 0.0%), real disposable income fell 0.3%, and saving rate was 3.8%. August income is now 0.3% and real spending 0.5%; original vintages remain preserved. Strong quarterly private demand and revised monthly core persistence oppose the slower quarterly inflation and softer September household real-income/spending figures. One combined package, not a count of components.

One policy package, not independent votes. Hold, target recognition and higher next-year inflation were broadly anticipated in the Reuters preview; no surprise December commitment or measured repricing claimed. Governor conference remains pending.

direction.reason: Slight strengthening retained after rechecking the corrected policy-path balance. Surprise October28 4-3 hold2.75%, majority weak pass-through, subdued wages, consumer confidence81.1 and major-purchase appetite-17 oppose strength. Breman October29 high December likelihood was already available. Full Reuters Silk interview supports a hike if CURRENT conditions persist, a lower hurdle than the earlier TE paraphrase. Reported76% December probability/3.75%-or-higher peak are dated attributed expectations, not new matched pricing or majority commitment. Conditional return to restraint and business pricing modestly outweigh extrapolating an old hold into continued selling; household weakness, risk and oil imports cap intensity. A patient majority or weak jobs/wages defeats strength. AUD has more direct documented AI/commodity cross vulnerability; the old AUDNZD buy is retired, without forcing a reverse trade. Equal GBP/NZD grades do not establish GBPNZD. Daly introduction is not a decisive missing NZ fact. Combined jobs/wages is the next primary domestic test of December pass-through, not three independent votes.
